caseLines.text: If you want a real starting QB for the stretch run, this is worth it. Prescott is a top QB on a good offense, and you still keep a TE. Your RB depth stays the same.
If you believe Flowers' slump is real and not a blip, selling him for Prescott makes sense. You fill your empty QB spot, but you thin out at WR. It is a gut call on whether your FLEX2 can be patched.
If you want real QB help now, this is worth it. Prescott fills your empty QB slot, and Unsolicited Dak Picks is out of the race and gets the better player.
If you believe Flowers keeps cooling off, this is worth it. You turn a fading WR into a top QB, and Unsolicited Dak Picks gets the better player.

If you want a starting QB without gutting your lineup, trading McBride for Stroud fills your biggest weak slot. You have no QB in the top 24 and Stroud is a top QB this season. Unsolicited Dak Picks is out of the race and gets the better player in McBride, so this is a deal they can say yes to.

If you believe Flowers is a fading piece, you can swap him for a QB1 and fill your empty QB slot. Flowers has cooled lately, and Unsolicited Dak Picks is out of the race and wants a WR to fill its depth. The cost is that your WR depth gets thinner.

If you'd rather have a QB who starts every week than a TE on a weak offense, this is worth it. You fill your empty QB spot with a top QB and still keep a top TE. Dak Picks is out of the race and fills a need at TE, so the other manager should say yes.

If you trust Stroud's recent form and don't mind giving up a TE on a weak offense, this works. It fills your empty QB slot, and the other manager gets the better player while out of the race. Stroud costs less than Prescott, so it is the second choice.

If you would rather have a steady QB than a TE on a weak offense, this is worth sending. You fill your empty QB spot and still keep a TE. Unsolicited Dak Picks is out of the race and wants the better player, so the other manager should say yes.
If you think Flowers' slump keeps going, selling him for Prescott is worth it. You get your QB, and the other manager needs WR help. Your second flex spot will be thin afterward.

If you want your QB spot fixed without giving up your TE spot, this is worth it. You turn a TE1 on a weak offense into a top QB on a strong one, and the other manager gets the better player for a lost season.
If you are fine paying a TE1 for a QB just below the top tier, this works as a QB fix. It is a step behind the Prescott deal, so only go here if that one is gone.
